claims.statement: If X has density cap L, is independent of a pair (C,D) of joint-density cap M, beta*gamma!=0, then 2 beta X C+alpha C^2+2 eta CD+gamma D^2+mu C+nu D+kappa has density cap 3(2LM)^(2/3)|beta^2 gamma|^(-1/3), uniformly in all other coefficients.

For original product Z, genuine independent scalar X, U=u.Z,V=v.Z, G=det Gram(u,v), and null-pivot form 2kU(gamma X+aU+bV+h0)+beta V^2+mU+nV+r with auxiliary-independent coefficients, ||p||inf <=3*4^(2/3)L_X^(2/3)[k^2 gamma^2 |beta| G]^(-1/3).
If h=a u+b v+w with w perpendicular to span(u,v), the null-pivot Z-quadratic matrix has exact rank three for w!=0 and signed pseudodeterminant -beta k^2 detGram(u,v)||w||^2.

For the exact rank-three transverse residual, if its entire-range coordinate leverage is <=1/32 and s is its smallest nonzero singular value, the full affine-restored conditional product-law form has a continuous density bounded by (96e/(7sqrt2))/s <27/s.

Adding a source-valid cap-one translated square a0(T+Psi)^2 to the in-plane base and applying completed account04/B18 gives density cap 2sqrt3*4^(1/3)L_X^(1/3)|a0|^(-1/2)[k^2 gamma^2 |beta| G]^(-1/6).

limitations: The in-plane theorem does not allow an arbitrary affine term transverse to span(u,v).
The transverse curvature theorem is for a linear shared translation h.Z; arbitrary nonlinear shared shifts are not covered.
The diffuse transverse exit requires the explicit <=1/32 entire-range leverage gate.
The pseudodeterminant identity alone does not lower-bound the smallest nonzero singular value.
No completed account04/B06 canonical theorem was available; account04/B18 was the compatible completed account04 result actually applied.
